native_interfaces.semantics_assumed: The active init/update/finalize path returns the standard BLAKE3 extendable-output hash of exactly the supplied bytes; a 32-byte request returns the standard 256-bit digest. The FFI respects Lean ownership, lifetime, array-size, and C-ABI contracts. Uncalled keyed, derive-key, and version exports are covered because importing Blake3.Rust makes them reachable to downstream Lean code, but Compilatr.ix does not currently rely on their results. The sibling Blake3.C module binds the vendored C implementation behind six c_blake3_* externs; Compilatr.ix does not import it, so they are inventoried as present-but-unimported and any drift in the package tree's extern set fails the check.
native_interfaces.proof_effect: Content addresses use this result operationally. There is no Lean theorem connecting the returned bytes to a pure BLAKE3 specification, so collision resistance and conformance are explicit assumptions rather than proved facts. Generic evaluator readdressing, HPT evaluator and case-binder-field concretization, owner-sensitive case pruning, exact scalar fetch forwarding, local PAP/application refinement, and the rooted-restriction fuel induction are hash-independent and remain in the ordinary logical axiom set, while the indexed production addressed-lowering, checked HPT cache/summary/accepted-result/consumer theorem cones, and public reachability theorems that validate an exact input digest intentionally expose Blake3.HasherOps.hash._native.native_decide.ax_1✝ because they consume actual native digests; Compilatrix/Fence.lean pins that exact exception. The opaque FFI declarations also cross a proof-bearing subtype boundary for output length. Canonical IxIR2 snapshot byte-codec laws use only existing logical axioms; addressed ingress and exact checked-source program/context recovery retain this same native hash exception, with an explicit pairwise collision premise for recovering artifact equality from root equality. Modular source context transport uses exact binding equality and only ordinary logical axioms; its assembled closed-source theorem retains the same production BLAKE3 dependency. Reuse also compares full finite contexts, and serialized source records reconstruct proofs through the ordinary checker. Indexed whole-program IxIR1 addressing proves exact equality with the original semantic and exact-source audit predicates, including malformed inputs. Its prepared lookup indexes retain first-binding precedence and reverse preimages; the returned compilation certificate and native hash exception are unchanged. Modular source preparation retains a proof of successful canonical-address validation only for exact owned entries, and shares a completed preparation within certificate production and checking. Full fresh-checker equality covers current context and policy rejection behavior; canonical facts do not replace dependency, usage, literal, or resource checks. Persisted records reconstruct canonical evidence afresh. Three additional exact fences retain the existing logical and native BLAKE3 basis; source queries, certificate bytes, native symbols, and native contracts are unchanged. The backend-independent checked Ixon erasure prefix exposes the same native hash dependency; Ixby lowering admission, total data equality, reference determinism, and fixed-input value/byte execution refinement introduce no new native boundary. Reusable Ixby symbolic substitution and value/byte reflection quantify over all admitted opaque-data argument arrays using only ordinary logical axioms; runtime data inspection remains outside the checked fragment.
trust_basis: The v3 checker also uses Blake3.Rust.Hasher.init, update and finalizeWithLength for tagged node and context preimages. They resolve to the same three active native symbols; no keyed or derive-key operation is used. An explicit kernel proof discharges the 32-byte output bound, and eight exact input/literal fences retain the existing axiom basis.

native_interfaces.semantics_assumed: On the x86_64-linux baseline, a successful regular-file call has opened a non-symlink regular file, completed fsync, and closed its descriptor; a successful directory call has done the corresponding type-checked fsync for the directory entry set. EINTR is retried. On Apple platforms the regular-file path first requests F_FULLFSYNC and falls back to fsync only when that operation is unsupported; directories use fsync. In every case the filesystem, kernel, and storage device truthfully implement the successful synchronization result, and the shim obeys Lean's borrowed-string and IO-result ABI.
native_interfaces.proof_effect: This boundary affects cache publication durability and availability only. Persisted HPT records remain untrusted bytes and cross the same bounded decoder, address checks, and ordinary certificate checker on every read, so no theorem or accepted compilation result assumes that sync succeeded semantically. A malicious shim could still corrupt arbitrary process state or filesystem data because it is native code.

Three spare continuations, 64 Nat bits and eight bytes suffice for every input representation. Both input Nat observations must fit the scalar limit; addition and multiplication also require the exact result to fit. Subtraction, division and remainder results are bounded by the left input, including a / 0 = 0 and a % 0 = a. Larger Nats are supported at larger limits. The stronger local native-field equality contract needs only five slots and no Nat, byte or additional continuation capacity. These are sufficient local contracts; ordinary whole-program admission separately validates all literals and functions.

The six base-field wrappers and extension packing have uniform local contracts with 11 slots, 64 Nat bits and three spare continuations. Each input Nat observation must fit the scalar limit. No byte buffer or additional result-capacity premise is required: asField constructs native fields from words and the results are canonical. These contracts preserve arbitrary caller continuations and retain complete program/input admission for whole-program evaluation.

The standalone shift and logarithm loops require at most six and five local slots respectively, two Nat bits for their literals, and no additional continuation or byte buffer. Shift inputs must fit; logarithm requires its input and accumulator plus final logarithm to fit. Public shift and logarithm need at most ten slots, 64 Nat bits, three spare continuations and eight bytes across all representations. Power and its loop need eleven slots, 64 Nat bits, four spare continuations and eight bytes. The public power inputs and result must fit; its accumulator starts at one. The internal loop permits arbitrary represented accumulators but additionally requires both the unscaled power and accumulated result to fit, as well as the inputs. Bounds are sufficient and independent of iteration count. Whole-program admission separately checks the complete image and inputs.

The compiler fixes USize width at 64 bits. Source contracts for USize.ofNat/add/sub state that platform premise explicitly; no axiom or native decision establishes it. Identity/comparison contracts use the exact source Nat view without a platform premise. The word test oracle checks that it is running on the 64-bit baseline.

Tree-backed array contracts require the live-prefix relation and a valid power-of-two Nat capacity, beyond structural input validation. Local sufficient bounds are 8 slots and no extra continuations for lookup, 12 slots and h continuations for tree writes, 10 slots and four continuations for public lookup, 12 slots and max(4,h+1) continuations for set!/uset, and 16 slots and max(4,h+2) for a growing push. Observed capacities/indices must fit, and doubling must fit when used. Numeric observations use 64 Nat bits and eight byte slots uniformly across representations; Array.usize needs 65 Nat bits and the explicit 64-bit platform premise. These are functional reference-machine limits, not a proving RAM model.
